terra.problem: The text does not say nobody finished their sentence.
Tiptoeing suggests Papa Dorin walks on his toes, but his gold base is part of him and always stays with him.
The text does not say the argument ended or that the scribes argued right up until Jesus arrived.
The disciples' private question does not establish that they wanted to drive the spirit out.
Calling Jesus' words a sigh adds a tone or reaction the text does not give.
The text does not say nobody in the crowd went home before the boy met Jesus.
The father says the spirit has been with the boy from childhood, but the passage does not establish how long that has been or rule out a recent start.
The passage does not establish how long ago the boy's childhood began, so it does not rule out a recent start.
The text does not say the echo makes the father stop and hear himself.
Saying the command covers the boy for good states a future outcome the passage does not report; Jesus commands the spirit never to enter him again.
Even as a guess, saying the whole crowd stops talking adds an event the text does not describe.
